summary: The fixed recipient searches show a small local point-placement improvement, with no principal-versus-atom target-coverage gain in the saved records. All 64 slots and the separate Root admission gates remain visible.
assessment: 56 of 64 planned search records returned. The raw final checker observations include 50 accepted target-proof occurrences and 6 point-search UNKNOWN outcomes; 8 slots were not dispatched because shared compiler/Native setup hit the absolute deadline. Whole admission remains a separate gate.

Raw Native-accepted target occurrences out of 16 planned slots per method: S0: 14; P0: 12; PA: 12; PP: 12. The two order labels repeat case targets and are not new theorems or stochastic replications.
Opaque equality control, point-placement attempts in order labels 0/1: PP: [10, 10]; PA: [13, 13]; P0: [13, 13]. These saved point counts show a small local principal-family placement improvement.
First quantified case, point-placement attempts in order labels 0/1: PA: [23, 23]; PP: [23, 23]; P0: [28, 28]. The shared improvement of PA and PP does not isolate a principal-abstraction benefit.

Every returned point search on the second equality case ends UNKNOWN within its unchanged local budget; conventional S0 has saved accepted proof observations there. The second quantified case has no dispatched method search, not eight proof rejections.

Saved returned pool packets: PA: 70 and PP: 142; selected ordering packets: PA: 40 and PP: 40. Larger returned packet counts are not proof gains or completed cluster executions. Exact preferred-placement events appear below, and may later be rolled back.
PA and PP accept exactly the same saved case/order target set here; no principal-versus-atom target-coverage gain is observed.

This is fixed selection, not RL training. All point methods share certified markings. There is no matched conventional principal-library arm or marking-off ablation, so these observations do not establish a GCTS-specific, RL or state-of-the-art advantage. Common setup differs from D15/D16; no cross-study timing speedup is claimed.
